title: GitHub Trending Summary - Daily - 2026-11-12
ranking_explanation: The ten selected non-fork repositories are ranked by the stars-today values displayed on GitHub Trending, in descending order. Total stars, primary languages, repository identity, and current default-branch commits were corroborated through GitHub Search and REST API results.
global_caveat: GitHub Trending gains are a point-in-time signal and may change after capture. Star gain reflects attention, not product quality or sustained adoption. README-based details were checked for the highest-priority repositories; no DeepWiki enrichment was needed.

sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time: 2026-11-12 17:34 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-12 through 2026-11-12. Ranking basis: Daily GitHub Trending star gains.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-facing developer tools and agent-ready interfaces dominated the standout momentum: Meta's Astryx led this capture with 1,789 stars today, while engineering skills and modern-web guidance also drew nearly 800 or more. A separate self-hosted personal-finance app was the second-largest gainer, so today's signal extends beyond AI tooling.

sections.title: meta/astryx
sections.description: A customizable, agent-ready React design system, grown inside Meta and now released as an open-source component and tooling suite.
sections.why_notable: The day's largest gain; its README describes 150+ accessible components, theming, and a CLI designed for both developers and coding agents.
sections.unique_caveat: The README labels the project beta.

sections.title: we-promise/sure
sections.description: A self-hostable personal-finance app for tracking finances and wealth.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest daily gain and a notable non-agent consumer-app signal; it is a community-maintained fork of the abandoned Maybe Finance project.
sections.unique_caveat: The README identifies Sure as a community fork of the now-abandoned Maybe Finance project.

sections.title: addyosmani/agent-skills
sections.description: A set of production-oriented engineering workflows and quality gates for AI coding agents.
sections.why_notable: One of today's strongest gains, packaging a define-plan-build-test-review-ship lifecycle into reusable agent commands and skills.
sections.unique_caveat: The README notes that installing an individual skill may omit shared repository-level reference files.

sections.title: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src
sections.description: Source for browser-platform guidance that helps coding agents favor modern web APIs and practices.
sections.why_notable: A major daily spike for agent context tooling, with CLI search/retrieval, legacy-pattern scanning, and curated browser guidance.

sections.title: Alishahryar1/free-claude-code
sections.description: A multi-harness and multi-provider coding setup spanning terminal, desktop, IDE, phone, and browser clients.
sections.why_notable: Brings together a broad coding-agent ecosystem and provider routing; the project says it supports free, paid, subscription, and local providers.
sections.unique_caveat: Provider availability and limits can change; the README says the project is independent and not affiliated with Anthropic.

sections.title: pookjw/HermesEnabler
sections.description: A utility that enables Hermès watch faces on Apple Watch devices.
sections.why_notable: A sharp, device-specific surge outside the dominant web and coding-agent themes.

sections.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot
sections.description: An open-source AI coworker framework that gives agents a browser, files, and tools, with actions decided in advance and recorded.
sections.why_notable: Represents the move from coding assistants to agents operating through a computer-like workspace; it supports AG-UI agents.

sections.title: ggml-org/llama.cpp
sections.description: LLM inference in C and C++.
sections.why_notable: A local-inference counterpoint to the agent-layer trend, with substantial ongoing interest in the underlying model runtime.

sections.title: QwenLM/qwen-code
sections.description: An open-source AI coding agent that runs in the terminal.
sections.why_notable: Shows continued demand for model-provider-backed coding agents distributed as command-line tools.

sections.title: nodejs/node
sections.why_notable: A foundational runtime remains among today's gaining repositories, alongside newer agent and frontend projects.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflow packaging: addyosmani/agent-skills turns engineering phases and quality gates into reusable agent commands; GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src supplies focused web-platform knowledge. Agents with tools and execution environments: QwenLM/qwen-code and Alishahryar1/free-claude-code focus on coding-agent access and provider choice, while CopilotKit/OpenBot gives agents browser, file, and tool access with action logging. Agent-ready frontend systems: meta/astryx pairs a customizable React design system with an agent-aware CLI and documentation. Local inference and durable foundations: ggml-org/llama.cpp is the local-inference representative; nodejs/node and pookjw/HermesEnabler show activity in established runtime and device-utility categories. Languages: TypeScript appears in four repositories; JavaScript in two; Python, Ruby, Objective-C, and C++ each appear once.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's clearest cluster is the tooling around coding agents: reusable workflows, curated context, agent-accessible interfaces, and provider/harness integration. Astryx's unusually large daily gain suggests that making interface systems agent-ready is also resonating, while Sure and HermesEnabler show that the day's attention was not limited to AI projects. Star gains measure GitHub attention, not product quality or sustained adoption.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily. Corroboration: GitHub Search API repository queries using <repo-name> in:name user:<owner> matched all ten repositories; GitHub REST repository and default-branch commit endpoints confirmed current metadata and SHAs. Ranked by daily stars-today values at 2026-11-12 17:34 UTC, descending; total stars, languages, and SHAs checked through GitHub REST API.
